caption:
Up to $60,000 from your own RRSP. Milton first-time buyers, read this.

The Home Buyers' Plan lets eligible first-time buyers withdraw up to $60,000 from their RRSP toward a home, and repay it to their RRSP over a 15-year period. Each spouse or partner can withdraw from their own RRSP. You need a written agreement to buy or build, and the first-time buyer test looks at whether you lived in a home you owned in the current or past four calendar years. Amounts not repaid on schedule are added to your income.

Source: Canada Revenue Agency, Home Buyers' Plan (canada.ca, page modified Jan 20, 2026). Eligibility rules apply. General information only, not tax, mortgage or legal advice.

Older Kitchener home? Ask these 3 first.

1) Electrical: what are the panel and wiring types, and when were they updated? 2) Water: has the basement ever had water, and is there a sump pump? 3) Permits: were past renovations done with permits?

Raise these with your home inspector and lawyer. General information only, not legal advice.

Guess the down payment on an $800K Brampton home.

Example only: $800,000 purchase, insured mortgage, 25-year amortization. The minimum down payment in Canada is 5% of the first $500,000 ($500,000 × 5% = $25,000) plus 10% of the portion above $500,000 ($300,000 × 10% = $30,000). Total: $55,000, about 6.9% of the price. (Plain 5% would be $40,000.)

Not included: mortgage insurance. On a $745,000 loan (93.1% of the price) the CMHC premium rate is 4.00%, or $29,800, usually added to the mortgage. Ontario sales tax on the premium must be paid in cash at closing, and closing costs are separate. Lenders also apply their own qualifying rules, including the stress test.

Sources: Government of Canada (Financial Consumer Agency of Canada), minimum down payment rules; CMHC, mortgage loan insurance premium table. Checked Oct 27, 2026. Estimates only; eligibility and lender rules apply. Not mortgage, tax or legal advice.

caption:
Oct 28 could raise your monthly mortgage. By how much?

The Bank of Canada announces its rate decision on Oct 28, 2026 (policy rate now 2.25%).
- Reuters poll: 19 of 34 economists expect a hike to 2.50%; markets moved from about a 30% chance to roughly three in four.
- Not everyone agrees: some economists, incl. National Bank's Stéfane Marion, argue against a hike now.
- Variable rate: your monthly mortgage could rise about $13 for every $100K you owe (example 3.43% to 3.68%, 25-year amortization; on a $500K mortgage that's about $66 more a month).
- Fixed rate: no change until renewal; fixed rates follow bond yields. Buying or renewing? Ask your lender about a rate hold.
- Selling: national sales were down 7.7% year over year in September; price from recent sold homes.

Sources: Reuters poll, Oct 23, 2026; MoneySense, Oct 22, 2026; Canadian Mortgage Professional, Oct 26, 2026; CREA (Sept 2026 data).
